Cause found: PR 132 re-anchors Windows `SUBST` paths too late, causing a safe repository to be rejected as off-volume.

On an Azure Windows VM, using CI’s synthetic merge commit `3f3dc249`, Go 1.26.6, and GCC 15.2.0, I reproduced:

```text
=== RUN   TestGitMetadataGuardAllowsSubstSubdirectoryRepository
provider_gitdir_unc_windows_test.go:1003:
    safe repository discovered from a SUBST subdirectory was refused
--- FAIL
TEST_EXIT=1
```

The control flow is:

1. The test aliases a physical directory as `Z:` and starts discovery under `Z:\checkout\subdir`.
2. [`lstat`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/321af0fb07678c3ca5d1e7ce4be3c9fa438e3084/internal/sem/provider.go#L11820-L11829) opens that directory and Windows canonicalizes it to its physical backing drive.
3. The resolver is still anchored to `Z:`, so comparing the physical path against that anchor returns `errSymlinkChainOffVolume`.
4. [`gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess`](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/321af0fb07678c3ca5d1e7ce4be3c9fa438e3084/internal/sem/provider.go#L13207-L13233) performs the bare-repository probe before switching to a physical resolver. It therefore returns `false` before reaching the new resolver-handoff block.

This is deterministic, not flaky. Junction coverage passes because the alias and target remain on the same drive. The likely minimal fix is moving the physical-resolver handoff before the bare-repository probe.
